Ingredient lists come from the extractor verbatim (a list of ingredients carries no copyright); the method prose here is our own. `cuisine` overrides the extractor's keyword guess. Only ids present in this file are built into src/data/sourceRecipes.js — add a tranche, re-run `npm run build:recipes`.

steps.title: Rub and load
steps.text: Mix the granulated garlic, pepper, dried thyme and salt, then pat it over every face of the roast. Put the carrots, onions and thyme sprigs in the bottom of a 4–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Brown the roast
steps.text: Get the oil hot in a sauté pan over medium-high and colour the roast on all sides — about 10 minutes in total. Set it on top of the vegetables.

steps.title: Build the sherry base
steps.text: Drop the anchovies and garlic into the same pan and cook a minute or two, until they smell like something. Pour in the sherry to lift the fond, bring it to a simmer, and tip the whole lot over the roast.

steps.title: Walk away
steps.text: Lid on. High for 4–5 hours, or low for 7–8 — it is done when a fork goes in without argument. Lift the roast and vegetables onto a plate, strain the liquid, and warm it in a small saucepan.

steps.title: Thicken and serve
steps.text: Whisk the cornstarch into cold water until there are no lumps, stir it into the hot liquid, and simmer until the sauce just coats a spoon. Pour over the roast and vegetables.

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Cover the beans with 6 cups of water in a pot, lid it, and leave it in the fridge overnight — 8 hours minimum.

steps.title: Parboil and skim
steps.text: Add the baking soda, bring the beans to a boil and hold a simmer for 10 minutes, lifting off any foam that rises. Drain, rinse, and move them to a 5–6 qt slow cooker with a fresh 6 cups of water.

steps.title: Sweat the aromatics
steps.text: Melt the butter in a sauté pan over medium-high and cook the onion, carrot and celery until they slump, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic for a final minute, then scrape it all into the cooker.

steps.title: The long part
steps.text: Bury the ham hock and bay leaf in the beans. Cover and cook until the beans give completely — 3½–4½ hours on high, 4½–5½ on low. Fish out the hock, strip the meat off the bone, discard the fat, and chop the meat.

steps.title: Finish thick
steps.text: Return the ham, season with salt and pepper, and stir in the potato flakes and parsley. Another 30 minutes covered and the soup will have body.

steps.title: Oven to 325°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 325°.

steps.title: Sear hard
steps.text: Sear the roast in oil in a Dutch oven over high heat until each side is deeply browned, roughly 5 minutes a face. Move it to a plate.

steps.title: Sweat the base
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium and cook the onion, diced carrot and celery in the drippings with the lid on until soft, 10–12 minutes. Stir the garlic through for the last 30 seconds.

steps.title: Bloom the paste
steps.text: Cook the tomato paste and Dijon for 2 minutes, then stir in the flour, cocoa and espresso powder and give it one more minute.

steps.title: Deglaze and return
steps.text: Pour in the wine and scrape the pan clean. Add the broth, rosemary and bay, bring it to a boil, settle the roast back in, cover, and move the pot to the oven.

steps.title: Three hours
steps.text: Braise 3 hours. Lift the roast out, strain the sauce and discard the spent vegetables and herbs, then return both sauce and roast to the pot.

steps.title: Add the roots
steps.text: Add the carrot pieces, shallots, parsnips and beets, cover, and braise another 1½ hours or so, until the meat gives to a fork. Transfer everything to a platter.

steps.title: Sharpen it
steps.text: Whisk the vinegar into the sauce and season with salt. (Hold back ½ cup of sauce and 8 oz of meat if you want beef sandwiches out of it later.)

steps.title: Marinate overnight
steps.text: Put the chuck, quartered onion, salt, garlic and peppercorns in a bowl, pour a whole bottle of wine over, cover, and chill 8 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Oven to 325°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 325°.

steps.title: Dry the meat
steps.text: Lift the chuck onto a paper-towel-lined tray, pat it properly dry, season with pepper, and throw the marinade away.

steps.title: Tie the sachet
steps.text: Bundle the thyme, rosemary and bay leaves into a square of cheesecloth and tie it shut.

steps.title: Bacon, then beef
steps.text: Crisp the bacon in a Dutch oven and lift it out. Brown the chuck in the drippings over medium-high for 10 minutes, then stir in the flour and cook another minute or two, moving it often.

steps.title: Deglaze with brandy
steps.text: Pour in the brandy and scrape up everything stuck to the base.

steps.title: Bring to a boil
steps.text: Add the broth, a cup of wine, the carrots and the herb sachet. Cover and bring the stew up to a boil.

steps.title: Into the oven
steps.text: Cook in the oven until the chuck is fork-tender, about 1½ hours. Stir in the green beans, pearl onions and tomatoes and give it 30 minutes more, until the beans are just short of soft. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Bag the spices
steps.text: Tie the coriander, cloves, star anise and cinnamon stick into a small mesh bag or a knot of cheesecloth, and drop it into a 6–8 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Soften the aromatics
steps.text: Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in oil over medium heat until soft and sweet, 7–9 minutes, then add them to the cooker.

steps.title: Fill the pot
steps.text: Add the pork with its bone, the broths, fish sauce, sugar and lemongrass. Top up with water until the liquid is nearly at the rim.

steps.title: Chill, then go long
steps.text: Leave it in the fridge overnight. When you're ready, lay the whole bunch of cilantro on top, cover, and cook until the pork falls apart — 8–10 hours high, 10–12 low.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour everything through a fine sieve into a large bowl. Bin the spice bag, cilantro and lemongrass; keep the pork.

steps.title: Season the broth
steps.text: Return the broth to the cooker on low and correct it with more fish sauce and sugar until it tastes finished.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.text: Divide the pork and rice noodles between bowls, ladle the hot broth over, and pile on the herbs and vegetables at the table.

steps.title: Dredge and sear
steps.text: Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high. Toss the beef in flour and sear it in two batches — another spoon of oil for the second — 3–5 minutes a batch, until properly browned.

steps.title: Mushrooms and paste
steps.text: Cook the mushrooms in the last spoon of oil in the same pan. Add the garlic for a minute, then the tomato paste, and let it darken for 3 minutes. Deglaze with 1 cup of the stock, scraping the pan clean.

steps.title: Layer, don't stir
steps.text: Layer the rutabaga, potatoes, carrots, parsnip, onions, bay and rosemary into a 4–6 qt slow cooker, then the beef and mushrooms on top. Pour the remaining 3 cups of stock in and leave it alone — no stirring. Cook 1 hour on high, then 3 hours on low.

steps.title: Beans and body
steps.text: Stir in the green beans and cook 30–40 minutes more, until tender. Pull out the rosemary and bay, stir in the potato flakes to thicken, and season.

steps.title: Oven to 450°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 450°.

steps.title: Bake the shells
steps.text: Rub the potato skins with oil, season them, and bake until a fork slides in easily, 45–60 minutes. Let them cool enough to handle.

steps.title: Bacon base
steps.text: Crisp the bacon in a large sauté pan, lift it out, and keep the drippings. Cook the scallion whites and garlic in that fat over medium heat for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Rice the filling
steps.text: Halve the potatoes lengthways and scoop out the flesh, leaving about ¼ inch behind so the skins hold. Push the flesh and the tofu through a ricer into a big bowl and add the bacon-fat mixture.

steps.title: Fill and brown
steps.text: Stir in 1 cup of the Parmesan, the sour cream and the milk, and season. Heap the filling back into the skins, set them in a baking dish, scatter the last ½ cup of Parmesan over, and bake 20 minutes until golden.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Chop the bacon, toss it with the scallion greens, and scatter over the top.

steps.title: Mix the rub
steps.text: Stir all the rub ingredients together in a bowl.

steps.title: Coat and sear
steps.text: Press the rub all over the pork, then sear it in oil in a large pan over medium-high until browned on every side, 8–10 minutes. Move it to a 4–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: Stir the first five sauce ingredients together.

steps.title: Deglaze
steps.text: Pour the jerk sauce into the hot pan over medium-high and scrape up everything stuck to the bottom. Stir in the tapioca, then pour it over the pork.

steps.title: Three hours
steps.text: Tuck the sweet potatoes around the roast, cover, and cook 3 hours on high. Lift the pork onto a board and the potatoes into a bowl; keep the sauce.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Add the milk, orange juice, butter, 1 Tbsp brown sugar, ¼ tsp allspice and ¼ tsp ginger to the potatoes and mash to a mostly-smooth mash. Salt to taste.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Slice the pork and serve it with the sauce and the mash.

steps.title: Soak and load
steps.text: Soak the beans as the packet directs, drain them, and put them in a 4–6 qt slow cooker with 6 cups of the broth.

steps.title: Render the pepperoni
steps.text: Brown the pepperoni in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high for 5 minutes, then drain it on paper towel and pour off the fat.

steps.title: Onion and heat
steps.text: Heat the oil in the same pan and cook the onion until it starts to colour, 5 minutes. Add the garlic and pepper flakes for a minute more. Scrape into the cooker along with the pepperoni and potatoes. Cover and cook until beans and potatoes are tender — 4 hours high, 6½ low.

steps.title: Wilt the kale
steps.text: Lay the kale over the top, pour in the last 2 cups of broth, cover, and give it 30 minutes more. Season with salt and more pepper flakes.

steps.title: Oven to 450°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 450° with a rack at the very bottom, and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Roast for romesco
steps.text: Roast the tomatoes, bell pepper and yellow onion on the lined sheet for 12 minutes.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Add the garlic and bread and roast 5 minutes; add the almonds and roast 4–5 minutes more, until golden. Slip the skins off the tomatoes, pepper and garlic. Blitz everything with the oil and vinegar until smooth, then season.

steps.title: Dry the potatoes
steps.text: Toss the potatoes and minced onion with 1 Tbsp salt and let them drain in a colander for 10 minutes. Spin them dry, then wring them out hard in kitchen towels — this is the step that decides whether they crisp.

steps.title: First side
steps.text: Melt 1 Tbsp butter in each of two 6½-inch cast-iron skillets over high heat. Split the potatoes between them, tamp them flat with a fork, and cook 1 minute. Drop to medium-low for 5 minutes, then turn each rösti out onto a plate.

steps.title: Second side, then oven
steps.text: Melt the last Tbsp of butter in each pan and slide the röstis back in cooked-side up. Two minutes on the hob, then 10 minutes in the oven; flip out onto plates, return upside down, and give them 10 minutes more.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with the romesco, eggs, ham, goat cheese and parsley.

steps.title: Oven to 200°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200° — it is only there to keep things warm later.

steps.title: Brown the chops
steps.text: Heat the oil in a 10-inch cast-iron skillet over high, brown the chops on both sides, and set them aside on a plate.

steps.title: Butter the pan
steps.text: Melt 2 Tbsp butter in the same skillet over low heat.

steps.title: In with the cabbage
steps.text: Stir in the cabbage, onion, fennel, cinnamon, kosher salt and bay leaf.

steps.title: Braise 20 minutes
steps.text: Whisk the wine, ½ cup apple juice, brown sugar and vinegar together and pour it in. Bring it to a simmer over low heat, sit the chops on the cabbage, clamp on a tight lid, and cook 20 minutes. Make the dumplings while it goes.

steps.title: Cut the dumpling dough
steps.text: Whisk the flour, chives, baking powder and table salt together, then cut the cubed butter in until the pieces are pea-sized.

steps.title: Bring it together
steps.text: Stir the applesauce, 2 Tbsp apple juice and egg together, then fork it into the flour just until it comes together — no further.

steps.title: Hold the chops
steps.text: Move the chops to a plate and park them in the warm oven. Stir the cherries into the cabbage and pull out the cinnamon stick and bay.

steps.title: Steam the dumplings
steps.text: Drop the batter onto the simmering cabbage in 2 Tbsp scoops, cover, and steam 15–18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out of a dumpling clean.

steps.title: Oven to 400°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 400° and line a baking sheet with foil.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Heat the oil in a sauté pan over medium-high, brown the beef on all sides in 3–5 minutes, and set it aside.

steps.title: Mushrooms and roux
steps.text: Melt the butter in the same pan over medium heat, season the mushrooms, and cook them until browned, 7–8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste, rosemary and garlic for a minute, then the flour for one more.

steps.title: Deglaze
steps.text: Pour in the brandy and scrape the pan clean, then whisk in the broth until it's smooth.

steps.title: Simmer the filling
steps.text: Add the potatoes and beef, bring it to a boil, then drop to medium and simmer covered for about 20 minutes, until beef and potato are nearly tender. Stir through the mixed vegetables, onions, parsley and red wine vinegar.

steps.title: Cut the lids
steps.text: Meanwhile cut the puff pastry to fit two 2-cup ovenproof bowls with a ¼-inch overhang — cut shapes from the offcuts if you like — and chill until needed.

steps.title: Cap the pies
steps.text: Ladle the stew into the bowls, lay the pastry over, and stretch and press the edges down over the lip. Egg-wash, add any cut-outs, egg-wash again, and cut a few vents. Set them on the foiled sheet.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 30–40 minutes, until the filling bubbles and the crust is golden; tent with foil if it colours too fast. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Press the tofu
steps.text: Set the tofu on a towel-covered rack in a baking sheet, lay another towel on top, and weigh it down with a 9×13 dish. Press 1 hour — longer is fine in the fridge — then cut it into 1-inch cubes.

steps.title: Oven to 450°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 450° with a baking sheet inside it.

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Whisk the oil, zest, lemon juice, mayonnaise, garlic, anchovy paste and Dijon together, then season.

steps.title: Roast tofu and bread
steps.text: Toss the tofu with ¼ cup of the dressing and the grated Parmesan, spread it on the hot sheet, and bake 10 minutes. Flip and give it 10 more, until golden. Brush both sides of the baguette slices with dressing and toast them on a separate sheet, about 7 minutes.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Toss the romaine, shaved Parmesan and roasted tofu with the rest of the dressing and serve with the toasts.

steps.title: Oven to 375°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 375° with a rack in the middle.

steps.title: Season the dredge
steps.text: Mix the flour, salt, cumin, chili powder and pepper in a shallow dish, then coat the chicken and shake off the excess. Keep the leftover flour.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Brown the chicken on both sides in two batches, a spoon of oil per batch, in a Dutch oven over medium-high — about 8 minutes. Set it aside.

steps.title: Sweat the base
steps.text: Cook the onion, celery, carrot, garlic, bay and chipotle in the last spoon of oil over medium heat until softened, 5 minutes.

steps.title: Deglaze and oven
steps.text: Deglaze with the wine and let it cook almost dry, then stir in the reserved dredging flour. Work in the broth and tomatoes gradually, cover, and cook in the oven for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Return the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken, beans, corn, oregano and lime juice, and bring it back to a simmer on the hob.

steps.title: Mix the dumplings
steps.text: Combine the flour, masa harina, green chiles, Parmesan, baking powder, salt and cayenne.

steps.title: Scoop and steam
steps.text: Warm the milk and butter until the butter melts and stir it into the dry mix. Roll into 2 Tbsp balls, sit them on the stew, cover, and return to the oven for about 20 minutes — a toothpick should come out of a dumpling clean.

steps.title: Brown the meats
steps.text: Brown the stew meat in oil in batches in a large skillet over medium-high, 5 minutes a batch, draining each onto paper towel. Do the kielbasa the same way, 3 minutes a batch.

steps.title: Deglaze with orange
steps.text: Pour the orange juice into the hot pan and scrape up every brown bit. Keep it.

steps.title: Four hours
steps.text: Put the onion, tomatoes, beans, garlic and chili powder in a 4–6 qt slow cooker, then stir in the browned meats and the orange deglaze. Cover and cook on high about 4 hours, until the beef gives to a fork.

steps.title: Sharpen and garnish
steps.text: Stir in the vinegar and season. Finish each bowl with sliced jalapeño, orange wedges and zest.

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Cover the peas with an inch of water and leave them in the fridge overnight. Drain and tip them into a 6–8 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Sear the chicken in oil in a large skillet over high heat until browned on both sides, about 7 minutes, and move it to the cooker. Drop the heat to medium-low.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: Soften the bell pepper and onion in the drippings for a minute, then the garlic and ginger for another. Add the tomato paste, fenugreek, cayenne, paprika, cumin, coriander, basil, cardamom, cloves, allspice and cinnamon and cook 1–2 minutes — this is where the whole dish gets its character.

steps.title: Deglaze
steps.text: Pour in the wine and cook it almost away, about a minute.

steps.title: Six hours
steps.text: Stir in the broth and tomatoes, bring to a boil, and pour it over everything in the cooker. Cover and cook 6 hours on either setting, until the peas are tender.

steps.title: Shred and finish
steps.text: Add the sweet potatoes and cook 15–30 minutes until tender. Pull the chicken out, strip the skin and bones, shred the meat and return it. Stir in the vinegar, season, and finish with cilantro.

steps.title: Oven to 425°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 425° with a baking sheet inside.

steps.title: Mix the meatballs
steps.text: Combine the chuck, pork, Parmesan, bread crumbs, yogurt, 3 Tbsp garlic, dried basil, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper.

steps.title: Roll and roast
steps.text: Roll 22 meatballs at about 1½ oz each and set them carefully on the hot sheet. Bake 20 minutes, turning them at the halfway mark.

steps.title: Start the sauce
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high and cook the onion, carrots, 3 Tbsp garlic, tomato paste, oregano and pepper flakes until lightly browned, 8–10 minutes. Move it to a 6–8 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Add the tomatoes
steps.text: Stir the tomatoes, tomato sauce and wine into the cooker.

steps.title: Nestle and go
steps.text: Settle the meatballs into the sauce, leaving their drippings behind. Cover and cook 3–4 hours on high or 5–6 on low. Skim the fat off the top and season with salt, pepper and a little sugar.

steps.title: Boil the pasta
steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in plenty of salted water as the packet says, drain, and serve under the meatballs and sauce with basil and Parmesan.

steps.title: Boil the pickle
steps.text: Boil the vinegar, water, maple syrup, cinnamon stick and black pepper together for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Pickle the onions
steps.text: Pour it over the onions, leave it to cool at room temperature for 20 minutes, then cover and chill. Give them at least 2 hours — they keep for months sealed in jars.

steps.title: Bacon, then beef
steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large sauté pan over medium-high and drain it, keeping 2 Tbsp of the fat. Brown the beef in the same pan, drain it in a sieve, and move it to a 4–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Toast the spices
steps.text: Cook the garlic, jalapeños, chili powder, mustard seed, oregano, cumin, cinnamon and cayenne in the bacon fat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until the spices smell toasted. Add that to the cooker with the salsa, beer, corn, tomatoes, barbecue sauce and bacon, stir once, and cook on low 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top each bowl with the pickled onions.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Poach the chicken and make the base, then dice 2 cups of the meat once it is cool enough to handle.

steps.title: Save the schmaltz
steps.text: Scrape the schmaltz-butter off the top of the chilled chicken base and keep it separate — it is the fat for everything that follows.

steps.title: Wet mix
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, club soda, shredded onion and 2 Tbsp of the schmaltz-butter together.

steps.title: Chill the dumplings
steps.text: Mix the matzo meal, dill, salt and baking powder, stir the egg mixture in just to combine, then cover and chill 30 minutes. Scoop 12 dumplings without compacting them, set them on a greased sheet, cover and chill until needed.

steps.title: Sweat the vegetables
steps.text: Cook the diced onion, carrot and celery in the last 2 Tbsp of schmaltz-butter over medium-low, covered, stirring now and then, until soft — about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Build the soup
steps.text: Stir in the reserved chicken base and the broth, bring it to a boil, then back down to a bare simmer and season.

steps.title: Poach and assemble
steps.text: Add the dumplings, cover, and simmer about 25 minutes until cooked through; lift them out. Warm the diced chicken through in the soup, stir in the parsley, and return the dumplings before serving.

steps.title: Oven to 475°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 475° with racks in the top and bottom thirds and two baking sheets heating inside.

steps.title: Spice the drumsticks
steps.text: Shake the curry powder together with 1 tsp each cumin, coriander, salt and pepper in a large resealable bag, add the drumsticks, and toss until coated.

steps.title: Spice the vegetables
steps.text: Toss the potatoes and cauliflower with the oil, 2 tsp each coriander, cumin and pepper, 1½ tsp salt and the turmeric.

steps.title: Roast on two sheets
steps.text: Drumsticks onto one hot sheet, vegetables onto the other. Roast 10 minutes, turn or stir, then 10–15 minutes more — the drumsticks want 175° at the bone and the vegetables want to be fork-tender. Finish with cilantro.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high and brown the beef in two batches, about 5 minutes each. Move it to a 4–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Cook the tomato paste and ginger in the pan for a minute, deglaze with the wine and reduce it by half, scraping as you go. Whisk in the broth, vinegar, gin, tapioca and salt and simmer 5 minutes. Pour it over the beef and submerge the spice sachet. Cover and cook on high until tender, 2½–3 hours.

steps.title: Vegetables and gingersnaps
steps.text: Add the carrots, celery and onion, then stir in the crushed gingersnaps — they are the thickener. Cover and cook about an hour more, stirring once halfway, until the sauce coats and the vegetables are tender.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Lift the beef and vegetables onto a dish, discard the sachet, and spoon the sauce over.

steps.title: Soak the bread
steps.text: Whisk ¼ cup cream with the egg in a large bowl, add the bread, and let it soak until saturated. Add the chuck, pork, onion, 1 tsp zest, ½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper, nutmeg and allspice, and mix lightly — overworking it makes them tough.

steps.title: Hide the cheese
steps.text: Scoop 12 scant ¼-cup portions, press a piece of cheese into each, and close the meat around it.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high and brown the meatballs for about 5 minutes, then drain them on paper towel.

steps.title: Slow cook
steps.text: Put the broth, Worcestershire and bay leaves in a 4–6 qt slow cooker and settle the meatballs in. Cover and cook 2–3 hours on high or 4–6 on low.

steps.title: Defat the liquid
steps.text: Lift the meatballs out and keep them warm. Pour the liquid into a fat separator, let it settle 5 minutes, and discard the fat.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium-high, whisk in the flour and cook 1–2 minutes until it thickens. Work in the defatted liquid gradually, add ¼ cup cream, bring to a boil and simmer about 5 minutes. Finish with lemon juice and season.

steps.title: Dress the noodles
steps.text: Toss the hot noodles with 1 Tbsp butter, the dill and 1 tsp zest, then season.

steps.title: Mince the base
steps.text: Blitz the onions, carrots and garlic to a mince in a food processor and set it aside.

steps.title: Sear the ribs
steps.text: Sear the ribs in 2 Tbsp oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high until browned on both sides, 7–10 minutes, then move them to a platter.

steps.title: Soften
steps.text: Add the minced vegetables, tomato paste, Italian seasoning and pepper flakes, season, and cook about 3 minutes until the onion softens.

steps.title: Three hours
steps.text: Deglaze with ¼ cup wine and cook it almost dry, 2 minutes. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato purée, bay leaf and Parmesan rind. Bring to a boil, return the ribs, cover, and simmer on low for 3 hours.

steps.title: Mix the meatballs
steps.text: Whisk the bread crumbs, grated Parmesan, milk, eggs, minced garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, black pepper and pepper flakes together, then fold in the chuck and pork gently. Shape about ten 3-oz meatballs, cover, and chill.

steps.title: Sear sausage and meatballs
steps.text: Brown the sausages in 2 Tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high, about 5 minutes, and set aside. Brown the meatballs in the drippings for 5 minutes and add them to the plate.

steps.title: Everything in
steps.text: Deglaze the skillet with the last ¼ cup wine, cooking it almost away, then add the sausages, meatballs and that wine to the Dutch oven.

steps.title: One hour more
steps.text: Simmer about an hour more, until the rib meat falls off the bone and the sausages and meatballs read 165°. Serve over spaghetti.

steps.title: Brown the roast
steps.text: Heat the oil in a sauté pan over medium-high and brown the roast on all sides, about 10 minutes. Move it to a 6–8 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Colour the vegetables
steps.text: Cook the carrots, celery, onions, garlic, rosemary, nutmeg, salt and pepper in the same pan until they start to brown, about 5 minutes. Add them to the cooker with the porcini sachet.

steps.title: Flour and paste
steps.text: Stir the flour and tomato paste into the pan and cook 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Six hours on low
steps.text: Deglaze with the stock, scraping up the browned bits, add the wine and bring it to a boil. Pour it into the cooker, cover, and cook on low 6 hours, until the meat is fork-tender. Lift the roast out, cover, and rest it 15–20 minutes.

steps.title: Chop the porcini
steps.text: Take the porcini out of the sachet, chop them, and set them aside.

steps.title: Strain and press
steps.text: Strain the braising liquid into a large bowl, pressing the vegetables against the sieve to get everything out of them.

steps.title: Reduce and serve
steps.text: Add the chopped porcini, transfer to a saucepan, skim the fat, and boil 10–15 minutes to reduce slightly. Slice the meat against the grain and serve with the sauce and cheesy sage polenta.

steps.title: Shake and brown
steps.text: Shake the flour, salt and pepper together in a paper bag, add the chicken and coat it. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high, brown the chicken meat-side down 2–3 minutes, flip for 1–2 more, and set it aside.

steps.title: Leeks and mushrooms
steps.text: Sweat the leeks and mushrooms in the same pan over medium heat until the leeks go soft, 3–4 minutes, adding oil if it looks dry. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.

steps.title: Into the cooker
steps.text: Deglaze with ½ cup wine and let it cook away, then add the remaining cup of wine and the broth. Bring it to a simmer and pour it into a 4–6 qt slow cooker. Stir in the carrots, potatoes and 6 thyme sprigs, lay the chicken on top meat-side up, cover, and cook on low 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Pull the meat
steps.text: Lift the chicken out to cool and discard the thyme. Once you can handle it, take the meat off the bones, stir it back in, and season.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Finish each bowl with bacon and a sprig of thyme.

steps.title: Tomatillo purée
steps.text: Blitz the tomatillos, chiles, onion and jalapeño smooth, then let it drain in a sieve until you need it and season with salt.

steps.title: Chorizo and beans
steps.text: Brown the chorizo in a nonstick skillet over medium-high for 5 minutes, stir the refried beans through, and set it aside.

steps.title: Custard
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, evaporated milk, corn and ½ cup of the cheese together and season.

steps.title: First layer
steps.text: Coat a round 2 qt slow cooker with nonstick spray and lay 2 tortillas in the bottom. Spread the chorizo mixture over them and add ½ cup cheese.

steps.title: Build up
steps.text: Layer on 2 more tortillas, the tomatillo mixture, and the last 2 tortillas, then pour the egg mixture over the lot.

steps.title: Cook until set
steps.text: Cover and cook on high 2½–3 hours, until the egg is firm. If liquid sits on top, leave it covered on warm for at least 15 minutes and it will reabsorb.

steps.title: Melt and finish
steps.text: Scatter the chips and the last cup of cheese over, cover, and let the cheese melt. Garnish with olives.

steps.title: Brown two at a time
steps.text: Heat the oil in a sauté pan over high and brown the shanks on both sides, two at a time, about 5 minutes. Move them to a 6–8 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Colour the vegetables
steps.text: Cook the onions, carrots, celery, garlic, rosemary, 1 Tbsp thyme, ½ tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper in the same pan until they begin to brown, about 5 minutes, then add them to the cooker.

steps.title: Flour and paste
steps.text: Stir the flour and tomato paste into the pan and cook 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Five hours
steps.text: Deglaze with the stock, scraping up the browned bits, add the wine and bring it to a boil, then stir in the tomatoes and pour it all into the cooker. Cover and cook on high about 5 hours, until the meat gives completely. Rest the shanks 15–20 minutes.

steps.title: Strain and skim
steps.text: Strain the braising liquid, pressing the vegetables against the sieve, skim off the fat, then bring the liquid to a boil in the sauté pan over medium-high.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Add the vinegar and reduce a little, then stir in 2 tsp thyme and season.

steps.title: Brown and spice
steps.text: Cook the chuck in oil in a pot over medium heat until it is cooked through, drain the fat, and return it with the onions, garlic, chili powder, cumin, oregano, coriander and cayenne. Drop to medium-low and cook partially covered for about 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onions are soft.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Stir in the broth, crushed tomatoes and vinegar, bring it to a boil, then simmer on medium-low for 10 minutes. Add the beans, diced tomatoes, cilantro and jalapeño and cook about 5 minutes more, until hot through. Season with salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top with cheese and red onion.

steps.title: Oven to 425°
steps.text: Heat the oven to 425° and spray a baking sheet.

steps.title: Blacken the poblanos
steps.text: Char the poblanos over a gas burner, or under the broiler 6 inches from the element, until the skins blacken. Put them in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let them steam 10 minutes — then the skin peels off in sheets.

steps.title: Open them up
steps.text: Cut a slit down one side of each and scrape out the seeds. Set them aside.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Boil the potatoes and onion in salted water until tender, about 7 minutes. Drain, return them to the pot, and stir over high heat for 30 seconds to drive off the water.

steps.title: Mash the filling
steps.text: Mash them with ¾ cup of the Jack, the scallions, cream cheese, green chiles, jalapeño, sour cream, garlic powder and cumin. Stir in the lime juice and season.

steps.title: Stuff
steps.text: Divide the filling between the poblanos and top each with some of the remaining ¼ cup of Jack.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake on the prepared sheet 20–25 minutes, until the cheese is golden.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Brown the chicken in oil in batches in a sauté pan over medium-high, about 10 minutes, then move it to a 4–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Onion, pepper, apple
steps.text: Cook the onion, bell pepper and apple in the same pan until they start to colour, about 5 minutes, and add them to the cooker.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: Cook the garlic, ginger, tomato paste, curry powder, garam masala, salt, black pepper and cayenne in the pan until fragrant, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Deglaze and cook
steps.text: Deglaze with the broth, scraping the base clean, then stir in the tomatoes and raisins and pour it over the chicken. Cover and cook until tender — 2 hours on high, 3 on low.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter almonds over each serving.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Cook the chicken in oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high until browned, 4–5 minutes, then move it to a 4–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Soften the peppers
steps.text: Cook the onion, bell pepper, piquanté peppers, garlic and ginger in the same pan until softened, about 5 minutes, and lay them over the chicken.

steps.title: Sweet-sour glaze
steps.text: Whisk the jelly, orange juice, lime juice, soy sauce, vinegar and 1 tsp agave together and add it to the pan. Bring it to a simmer, whisk in the tapioca, and pour it into the cooker.

steps.title: Spice bag on top
steps.text: Put the pickling spices in a large spice bag, sit it on top, and season. Cover and cook 2 hours on high or 3–4 on low.

steps.title: Adjust the heat
steps.text: If it comes out hotter than you want, stir in the chicken broth and another tsp of agave to soften it.

steps.title: Sear the roast
steps.text: Melt the butter with the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Put the pork in fat-side down and leave it to brown, 3–4 minutes, then colour the remaining sides — about 5 minutes more. Move it to the slow cooker.

steps.title: Milk, then two hours
steps.text: Deglaze the skillet with the wine, scraping it clean. Add the milk, cream, porcini, anchovy paste, pepper flakes and zest and simmer 3 minutes — the milk will look curdled and that is correct. Pour it around the pork, push the rosemary and sage under, cover, and cook on low about 2 hours, to 145° at the thickest point. Rest the pork under foil and fish out the herbs.

steps.title: Blend the sauce
steps.text: Blitz the sauce smooth in the cooker with a stick blender — that is what turns the split milk into a sauce — then season.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Slice the pork and spoon the sauce over.

steps.title: Make the paste
steps.text: Strip the reedy tops and root end off the lemongrass, then slice and mince about 4 inches up from the root. Blitz it with the onion, cilantro, ginger, fish sauce, jalapeño, garlic, coriander, sugar and zest to a paste. Scrape it into a 4–6 qt slow cooker and stir the coconut milk through.

steps.title: Brown and braise
steps.text: Brown the chicken in oil in a sauté pan, six pieces at a time, and add it to the cooker. Cover and cook 1½–2 hours on high or about 3 on low. Stir in the bell pepper and give it 15 minutes more on high.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter basil and peanuts over each bowl.

steps.title: Mix the seasoning
steps.text: Stir the cumin, paprika, onion powder, oregano, salt, coriander, garlic powder, black pepper, pepper flakes, ginger and cayenne together and set it aside.

steps.title: Brown in two batches
steps.text: Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high and brown half the meat; move it to a 4–6 qt slow cooker. Brown the rest in another spoon of oil and add that too. Deglaze the pot with the tequila, scraping up everything on the bottom, and pour that in as well.

steps.title: Four hours
steps.text: Add the tomatoes, bell peppers, diced onion, garlic and the fajita seasoning. Stir in the broth and flour, cover, and cook 4 hours on high.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir the beans and lime juice through just before serving. Sour cream, cilantro, avocado and sliced jalapeños on top if you want them.

steps.title: Mash the potatoes
steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water until a fork goes in, 12–15 minutes. Drain, return them to the dry pot, and stir over low heat for a minute to drive off the water. Mash with the sour cream, butter and milk until smooth, salt, and keep warm.

steps.title: Slurry the gravy
steps.text: Whisk the broth and flour together so there are no lumps before anything hot is involved.

steps.title: Build the gravy
steps.text: Melt 1 Tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium until it foams, cook the rosemary in it for a minute, then take the rosemary out. Whisk in the broth mixture and the reserved pot-roast sauce and simmer 5–7 minutes until it thickens. Stir in the vinegar and the reserved pot roast, heat it through, season, and keep it warm.

steps.title: Heat the broiler
steps.text: Broiler to high with a rack 6 inches from the element, and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Garlic butter
steps.text: Mash a stick of butter with the garlic and season it. Spread a tablespoon on each side of the toast slices and lay them on the sheet.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Broil until golden, about 2 minutes a side.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Pile the mashed potato onto the toast, ladle the beef gravy over, and finish with parsley.

steps.title: Load the cooker
steps.text: Put the tomatoes, onions, garlic, olives, Italian seasoning, pepper, fennel seeds, salt and bay leaf in a 4–6 qt slow cooker and stir.

steps.title: Nestle and go
steps.text: Settle the chicken down into the tomatoes, cover, and cook until it is cooked through and gives to a fork — 3 hours high, 6 low.

steps.title: Reduce the sauce
steps.text: Lift the chicken out and keep it warm; discard the bay. Tip the tomato mixture into a pot and bring it to a boil.

steps.title: Cook the tortellini in it
steps.text: Stir in the tomato paste and the tortellini and boil 7–9 minutes, until the pasta is al dente — it cooks in the sauce, so the sauce thickens as it goes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the sauce over the chicken and finish with parsley and Parmesan.

steps.title: Bed of vegetables
steps.text: Layer the onion, bell pepper and carrot into a 4–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Pound the steak
steps.text: Working one piece at a time between two sheets of plastic wrap, pound the steak out to ½ inch.

steps.title: Dredge
steps.text: Season ½ cup flour in a shallow dish and turn the beef through it, shaking off what doesn't stick.

steps.title: Sear in batches
steps.text: Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large pan over medium-high and sear the beef in two batches, 3 minutes a side, adding the second spoon of oil as needed.

steps.title: Four hours
steps.text: Lay the beef on the vegetables, pour in the broth and tomatoes, cover, and cook 4–4½ hours on high until fork-tender. Tent the beef under foil, lift the vegetables out with a slotted spoon, and take ⅓ cup of the liquid.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Whisk 1 Tbsp flour into that reserved liquid, then whisk it back into the cooker to make the gravy.

steps.title: Crisp the bacon
steps.text: Cook the bacon in a saucepan until crisp, drain it on paper towel, and pour off all but 1 Tbsp of the fat.

steps.title: Simmer the beans
steps.text: Cook the diced red onion, adobo sauce, garlic, ½ tsp cumin and the chili powder in that fat over medium-high until the onion softens, 3–5 minutes. Add the beans with their liquid, drop to medium-low, and simmer about 10 minutes until thick. Stir in 2 Tbsp lime juice and the bacon, then season.

steps.title: Mix the relish
steps.text: Combine the tomatoes, radishes, sliced red onion, jalapeño, minced cilantro, 1 Tbsp lime juice, oil and a pinch of cumin, and season.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Spoon the beans into the tortillas and top with the relish, sliced avocado, queso fresco and cilantro leaves. Lime wedges at the table.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Cook the rice as the packet directs, then leave it covered off the heat for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Season it
steps.text: Stir the vinegar and mirin through the rice, salt it, and keep it warm.

steps.title: Bloom the aromatics
steps.text: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium and cook the garlic, ginger and chili powder for a minute.

steps.title: Glaze the beans
steps.text: Deglaze with the soy sauce and let it reduce by half, 2–3 minutes. Add the beans and heat them through, 2–3 minutes. Stir in the cilantro and fold the lot into the rice.

steps.title: Sweat, then brown
steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot over medium and sweat the onions until soft, 3–4 minutes. Add the garlic for a minute, then the pork, and cook until browned, 3–4 minutes.

steps.title: Deglaze and simmer
steps.text: Pour in the wine, scrape the pot clean, and cook it until nearly dry. Stir in the broth, tomato sauce, Roma tomato and olives, bring it to a boil over medium-high, then drop to medium-low and simmer 10 minutes.

steps.title: Wilt and finish
steps.text: Stir in the spinach and beans until the spinach collapses, then season.

steps.title: Brown the sausages
steps.text: Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high and brown the sausages, 5 minutes a side. Set them aside to cool a little.

steps.title: Peppers, then onion
steps.text: Heat 2 Tbsp oil in the same pan and cook the peppers until softened, 4–5 minutes; move them to a 4–6 qt slow cooker. Heat the last spoon of oil and cook the onion and mushrooms 3–4 minutes, add the garlic for one more, and add those too.

steps.title: Sauce and slow cook
steps.text: Mix the marinara, tomato paste, thyme, rosemary and oregano and pour it in. Cover and cook 2–3 hours on high or 4–6 on low.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Put the sausages in the buns with about ½ cup of the pepper mixture and a slice of cheese over the top.

steps.title: Soak the beans
steps.text: Soak the beans as the packet directs, drain them, and put them in a 5–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Four and a half hours
steps.text: Add the broth, tomatillos, Anaheims, onions, jalapeños, garlic, cumin, oregano and coriander. Cover and cook about 4½ hours on high, until the beans are properly tender — dried beans will not soften once anything acidic is doing the work, so give them the full time.

steps.title: Chicken and masa
steps.text: Stir the chicken and masa harina in and cook 30 minutes more; the masa is the thickener and it needs that time to lose its raw edge. Finish with lime juice and season.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Lime wedges, sour cream and cilantro on top.

steps.title: Mix the marinade
steps.text: Combine the yogurt, lemon juice, 1 Tbsp garlic, 1 Tbsp ginger, ½ tsp salt, ½ tsp garam masala, the cumin, coriander and cayenne.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Stab the chicken all over so the marinade gets in, put it in a large bowl, pour the marinade over and turn it to coat. Cover and chill at least an hour, overnight if you can.

steps.title: Heat the broiler
steps.text: Broiler on, rack 6–8 inches from the element.

steps.title: Char the chicken
steps.text: Lift the chicken out and throw the marinade away. Broil it flesh-side up for 8 minutes — you want colour, not doneness — then move it to a 4–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Start the sauce
steps.text: Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high.

steps.title: Onion and spice
steps.text: Cook the onion until it just starts to colour, 5 minutes. Add 2 tsp garam masala, 1½ tsp garlic, 1½ tsp ginger and the serrano and cook a minute, then the tomato paste for one more.

steps.title: Deglaze with tomatoes
steps.text: Pour the tomatoes in and scrape up everything stuck to the pan, then tip it into the cooker and stir to coat the chicken.

steps.title: Three hours
steps.text: Cover and cook on low 3 hours, until tender. Lift the chicken onto a platter.

steps.title: Cream and serve
steps.text: Whisk the cream into the sauce and season, then pour it over the chicken and finish with cilantro.

steps.title: Render the bacon
steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large pot until crisp, about 8 minutes, and lift it out with a slotted spoon. Keep ¼ cup of the drippings.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Sear the chicken on both sides in 2 Tbsp of the drippings over medium-high, 2 minutes a side, and set it aside. Warm the other 2 Tbsp in the pot.

steps.title: Onion and roux
steps.text: Cook 2 cups of onion until softened, 4 minutes, then the garlic for a minute. Stir the flour in and cook it out for 2 minutes so it loses its raw taste.

steps.title: Build the pot
steps.text: Add 8 cups broth, the thyme, ½ tsp salt, cayenne, bay leaves and the seared chicken with everything it leaked, and bring it to a boil.

steps.title: Two hours of greens
steps.text: Stir in the greens, drop the heat to low, and simmer about 2 hours until they are completely tender. This is the whole dish — the greens are the point, not a garnish.

steps.title: Finish and thicken
steps.text: Stir in the parsley, lemon juice, Tabasco and filé, season, and simmer 5 minutes to thicken. Pull out the bay leaves.

steps.title: Trinity rice
steps.text: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium-high and cook ½ cup onion, the celery and bell pepper 2–3 minutes, then stir the rice in. Add the water, 1 cup broth and 1 tsp salt, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low 20 minutes. Rest it off the heat 5 minutes and fork it through.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Gumbo over rice, with tomatoes, scallions and the reserved bacon on top.

steps.title: Blitz the green base
steps.text: Blend the tomatillos, poblanos, serranos, garlic, onion, oregano, anise seed, cumin and lime juice until the tomatillos and onion are finely chopped. Pour it into a 4–6 qt slow cooker with the broth and stir.

steps.title: Add the bulk
steps.text: Add the fennel, hominy, garbanzo beans and sugar.

steps.title: Long and low
steps.text: Cover and cook 4–5 hours on high or 6–8 on low.

steps.title: Greens last
steps.text: Stir in the spinach and black beans and give it 2–3 minutes, just until the spinach wilts. Season.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Finish each bowl with pepitas, crispy cumin shallots, cilantro, lime and queso fresco.

steps.title: Par-cook the shells
steps.text: Boil the shells in well-salted water just until they bend without tearing, 8–9 minutes. Drain, rinse cold to stop them, and drain again.

steps.title: Mince the soffritto
steps.text: Mince the pancetta in a food processor and tip it into a bowl. Pulse the onions, carrot, celery and garlic in the same bowl of the processor until finely minced.

steps.title: Render the pancetta
steps.text: Cook the pancetta in a saucepan over medium until crisp, 8–9 minutes, and lift it onto paper towel. Raise the heat to medium-high.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Cook the soffritto in the rendered fat until it softens and goes dry, about 5 minutes, then add the tomato paste and rosemary for a minute.

steps.title: Wine, then tomatoes
steps.text: Deglaze with the wine and cook it almost away, 3 minutes. Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer on medium-low for 10 minutes, then stir in the vinegar and season.

steps.title: Line the dish
steps.text: Oven to 400°. Spray a 9×13-inch dish and spread half the sauce across the bottom.

steps.title: Fill, bake, rest
steps.text: Beat the ricotta, grated Parmesan, parsley, grated garlic and egg together with a hand mixer and season. Stuff each shell with a rounded tablespoon and set them cheese-side up in the dish, then pour the rest of the sauce over. Bake 25 minutes, until it bubbles at the edges. Rest 10 minutes and finish with the pancetta and shaved Parmesan.

steps.title: Grind the picada
steps.text: Pulse the bread crumbs, 2 Tbsp almonds, pine nuts, garlic, cumin, paprika, chili powder and pepper flakes in a food processor until minced — this is the thickener, so it should be sandy, not paste. Scrape it into a 4–6 qt slow cooker and stir in the onion, broth and sherry.

steps.title: Brown, then walk away
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high. Season the chicken and brown it on all sides, 5 minutes, then move it to the cooker. Cover and cook 2–3 hours on high or 4–5 on low. Lift the chicken out and keep it warm.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Stir the cream and vinegar into the cooker until the sauce comes together.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Almonds, lime wedges and cilantro over each plate.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.text: Brown the sausage in 2 Tbsp oil in a sauté pan over medium-high, 5 minutes, and move it to a 4–6 qt slow cooker. Pour off the drippings and wipe the pan.

steps.title: Peanut-butter roux
steps.text: Cook the flour and ½ cup oil in that pan over medium-high, stirring the whole time, until it is the colour of peanut butter, 7–10 minutes — stop stirring and it burns. Add the onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic, cayenne, black pepper and pepper flakes and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the broth and tip the lot into the cooker.

steps.title: Three and a half hours
steps.text: Stir in the turkey and tomatoes, cover, and cook 3½ hours on high or 5½ on low.

steps.title: Okra last
steps.text: Add the okra, parsley and thyme and give it 30 minutes more.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Season and spoon over white rice, with scallion and red bell pepper on top.

steps.title: Whisk the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the ketchup, vinegar, ¼ cup brown sugar, mustard, lemon juice, Worcestershire and soy sauce together, season, and set it aside.

steps.title: Mix the rub
steps.text: Combine the garlic powder, 1 Tbsp brown sugar, chili powder, 1 tsp salt and thyme.

steps.title: Rub and slow cook
steps.text: Pat the rub all over the chicken and put it in a 4–6 qt slow cooker. Scatter the onions over and pour 1 cup of the sauce on top. Cover and cook until tender, 3½ hours on high or 5 on low.

steps.title: Ditch the liquid
steps.text: Move the chicken and onions to a bowl and throw out what is left in the cooker — it is thin and greasy, and the reserved sauce is better.

steps.title: Shred hot
steps.text: Pull the chicken apart while it is still hot, discarding the bones, and return it with the onions to the cooker on warm. Toss with the last ½ cup of sauce.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile onto rolls and top with quick coleslaw.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Oven to 375° and spray a 2-cup baking dish.

steps.title: Infuse the cream
steps.text: Bring the cream, milk and garlic to a boil in a saucepan over medium and season it.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Lay a layer of potatoes in the dish, season, and add ½ tsp thyme; repeat. Pour over half the cream and add ¼ cup Gruyère and 1 Tbsp Parmesan. Do two more rounds of potato, seasoning and thyme, then finish with the last of the cream, Gruyère and Parmesan. Cover with foil.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: 45 minutes covered, then 15 more uncovered until the cheese browns. Rest 5 minutes.

steps.title: Low oven
steps.text: Oven to 300° — low and slow is the whole point with short ribs.

steps.title: Brown the ribs
steps.text: Heat ¼ cup oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, brown the ribs on all sides, 8–10 minutes, and set them on a plate. Drop the heat to medium-low.

steps.title: Sweat the base
steps.text: Sweat the onions, carrot and celery in the drippings until soft, 6–7 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika, tomato paste, anchovy paste and bay leaf for 2 minutes more.

steps.title: Sherry
steps.text: Deglaze with the sherry and cook it nearly dry, 5 minutes.

steps.title: Cola and wine
steps.text: Stir in the cola, wine and the zest of one orange, return the ribs, bring it to a boil over high, then lid it tightly and move it to the oven.

steps.title: Three and a half hours
steps.text: Braise until the meat gives to a fork, about 3½ hours, turning the ribs each hour. Tent them under foil.

steps.title: Strain and skim
steps.text: Strain the braising liquid and discard the solids. Skim the fat off the top, pour it into a sauté pan, and bring it to a simmer over medium.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Whisk the cornstarch with 2 tsp oil, whisk that into the liquid, and cook 2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the vinegar, thyme and minced zest, then warm the ribs through in the sauce, 5 minutes.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Oven to 400° and spray a 4-qt baking dish.

steps.title: Crumble the sausage
steps.text: Cook the sausage in oil in a saucepan over medium, crushing it with a potato masher until fine and cooked through, 5–7 minutes, then set it aside.

steps.title: Sweat the onions
steps.text: Sweat the onions, garlic, Italian seasoning and pepper flakes in the drippings over medium, covered and stirred now and then, until the onions soften, 10 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer and enrich
steps.text: Add the tomatoes and the sausage, simmer 15 minutes, then cool 15. Stir the mascarpone through and season — it goes in off the boil so it does not split.

steps.title: Undercook the pasta
steps.text: Boil the ziti in salted water for 8 minutes only; it finishes in the oven. Drain.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Toss the sauce, ziti and provolone together, tip it into the dish, and dust with Parmesan.

steps.title: Bake and rest
steps.text: About 30 minutes, until it bubbles at the edges. Rest 20 minutes before cutting.

steps.title: Sauce first
steps.text: Simmer the tamarind, brown sugar, fish sauce and sambal in a small saucepan over low for 5 minutes and set it aside.

steps.title: Soften the noodles
steps.text: Soak the noodles in very hot water just until pliable — not soft — and drain.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Cook the scallion whites and garlic until they start to colour, 2–3 minutes, then stir in the eggs and cook until lightly scrambled, 1–2 minutes. Set them aside and wipe the pan.

steps.title: Shrimp, then noodles
steps.text: Heat 1 Tbsp oil in the same pan and cook the shrimp until pink and curling, 2–3 minutes; set aside. Heat the last spoon of oil, add the noodles, stir the sauce through, and cook until the noodles drink it up, 3–5 minutes.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Toss the scallion greens, carrot, bean sprouts, egg and shrimp through the noodles. Peanuts, cilantro and lime wedges over each bowl.

steps.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps.text: Sauté the mushrooms in melted butter over medium-high until browned, 8–10 minutes, then add the garlic for 2–3 minutes more.

steps.title: Flour and wine
steps.text: Stir in the all-purpose flour and herbes de Provence and cook 1–2 minutes, then deglaze with the wine and season.

steps.title: Slow cook
steps.text: Add the mushroom mixture, carrots, leeks, celery, broth and applesauce to a 4–6 qt slow cooker and stir. Cover and cook 3 hours on high or 4–5 on low, then stir in the chicken and peas.

steps.title: Warm the milk
steps.text: Heat the milk with 2 Tbsp butter in a small pan until the butter melts.

steps.title: Mix the dumplings
steps.text: Whisk the cake flour, baking powder, 1 tsp salt, dry mustard and thyme together, then stir the milk in just until no flour shows — overworking it makes them tough.

steps.title: Drop and steam
steps.text: Drop rounded tablespoons of the dough into the cooker, cover, and cook 35 minutes, until the centres are no longer doughy.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Parsley and celery leaves over each bowl.

steps.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps.text: Melt 3 Tbsp butter in a sauté pan over medium. Season the mushrooms and cook until browned and nearly dry, 7–8 minutes, then set them aside.

steps.title: Sweat the base
steps.text: Sweat the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the last 2 Tbsp butter, covered, over low until soft, 3–5 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the noodles in the broth
steps.text: Add the broth, bring it to a boil over medium-high, stir in the noodles, and simmer on medium about 20 minutes until tender.

steps.title: Thicken and finish
steps.text: Shake the half-and-half and flour smooth in a screw-top jar — that is the reliable way to avoid lumps — and stir it in. Add the chicken, peas and mushrooms and cook until the stew thickens and bubbles, about 5 minutes. Stir in the thyme and chives and season.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Boil the broth in a saucepan over high, stir in the rice, cover, drop to low, and cook 15 minutes. Stand it 5 minutes, then fork it through with the parsley and scallions.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: Sauté the onion in oil in a saucepan over medium-high until soft, 3 minutes, then add the garlic, oregano, cumin, ¼ tsp salt and pepper flakes for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Simmer the beans
steps.text: Stir in the beans, tomato sauce and vinegar, bring to a boil, and simmer 3 minutes until thick. Season and spoon over the rice.

steps.title: Make the chowchow
steps.text: Simmer the mustard, ketchup, barbecue sauce and maple syrup in a saucepan over medium-low for a minute, then stir in the onion, relish and bell pepper and set it aside.

steps.title: Butter and toast
steps.text: Butter both sides of the bread and toast it on both sides in a large nonstick skillet over medium.

steps.title: Fry the sausage
steps.text: Press the sausage into a ¼-inch patty and fry it over medium-high until cooked through, 4–5 minutes a side. Keep it warm.

steps.title: Eggs in the drippings
steps.text: Crack the eggs into the same pan, season, and cook over medium until the whites are nearly set. Flip, cook until the yolks just start to set, lay the cheese over, and cover until it melts.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Halve the sausage, divide it and the eggs over two slices of toast, spoon the chowchow on, close the sandwiches and cut them in half.

steps.title: Dry the bread
steps.text: Spread the bread on a baking sheet and leave it until completely dry — fresh bread turns to mush in a strata.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Oven to 375° and spray a 9×13-inch dish.

steps.title: Brown the kielbasa
steps.text: Brown the kielbasa in oil in a large skillet over high, 3–5 minutes, and drain it on paper towel, keeping the drippings. Drop to medium and cook the onions and garlic in the fat 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, cream, broth, mustard, chives, thyme, salt and pepper together, add the bread and toss it to coat. Fold in the kielbasa, onions and half the Gruyère, transfer to the dish, cover, and refrigerate overnight. The overnight soak is the recipe — it cannot be rushed.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Scatter the remaining Gruyère over and bake about 45 minutes, to 160° in the centre. Rest 15 minutes.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Oven to 350° and spray a 3-qt baking dish.

steps.title: Blanch the noodles
steps.text: Blanch the noodles in boiling salted water for one minute only, drain, and rinse cold to stop them cooking. They finish in the oven.

steps.title: Sweat the vegetables
steps.text: Melt the butter in the same pot over medium, add the onions, carrots, celery and thyme, and sweat covered until soft, 5 minutes.

steps.title: Roux and wine
steps.text: Stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the wine and cook it away, 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Stir in the broth and cream, bring to a boil, then simmer until thick, 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Fold in the noodles, turkey, Cheddar, peas, parsley and lemon juice and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg. Tip it into the dish.

steps.title: Crumb and bake
steps.text: Mix the Parmesan, panko, melted butter, parsley and zest, season, and scatter it over. Bake 25–30 minutes until bubbling and brown, then rest 5–10 minutes on a rack.

steps.title: Two-zone grill
steps.text: Set the grill up with one side medium-high and the other medium-low, and oil the grate. Everything here needs one heat or the other.

steps.title: Vinaigrette
steps.text: Purée the vinegar, ¼ cup oil, capers, garlic, anchovy paste, Dijon and oregano in a mini food processor and season.

steps.title: Oil everything
steps.text: Brush the baguette slices, sausages, bell peppers and onion slices with ¼ cup oil.

steps.title: Char the peppers
steps.text: Grill the peppers over medium-high, covered, until soft and blackened all over, about 15 minutes. Bowl them under plastic wrap for 10–15 minutes, then peel, seed and chop.

steps.title: Sausages on the cool side
steps.text: Meanwhile grill the sausages over medium-low until charred and 155° in the centre, 10–15 minutes. Rest 5–10 minutes and cut into 1-inch pieces.

steps.title: Onions and bread
steps.text: Grill the onions over medium-high until soft, 4–6 minutes a side, and the baguette about 2 minutes a side. Rub the cut garlic over both sides of the bread, then cube it and chop the onions.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Toss the romaine, tomatoes, fontina, bread, sausages, peppers and onions with the vinaigrette.

steps.title: Butter the dish
steps.text: Lightly butter a 9×13-inch baking dish.

steps.title: Roux
steps.text: Melt 4 Tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium until it foams, whisk the flour in, and cook it 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Dijon béchamel
steps.text: Whisk 2 cups milk in slowly until smooth, then the Dijon and nutmeg, and season with salt and cayenne. Drop to medium-low and cook until it coats a spoon and a finger drawn through leaves a trail, 4–6 minutes.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread about ½ cup of béchamel across the bottom of the dish, then a third of the bread, half the ham, and another ½ cup of béchamel. Repeat, then finish with the last of the bread and the last ½ cup of béchamel.

steps.title: Custard and chill
steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the remaining 1½ cups milk and the black pepper, pour it over, and scatter the remaining cheese on top. Cover, weigh it down so the bread soaks evenly, and chill at least 4 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Take the chill off
steps.text: Oven to 375°. Let the strata sit out about 30 minutes and pull the wrap off.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: 60–75 minutes, until browned and bubbling and 160° in the centre, tenting with foil if it colours too fast. Stand 10–15 minutes, then parsley over the top.

steps.title: Mix and rest the masa
steps.text: Whisk the masa harina, ¾ tsp salt and baking powder together, then stir the water in. Cover the dough with a towel and let it rest 15 minutes so the masa hydrates.

steps.title: Shape the shells
steps.text: Divide the dough into 12 balls. Press each between two sheets of plastic wrap into a ¼-inch disc, then pinch a lip around the edge — that rim is what holds the filling.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat 1½ inches of oil in a cast-iron skillet to 350°. Fry the discs in batches, turning once, until golden and crisp, about 4 minutes. Drain on paper towel and keep them under a towel.

steps.title: Cook the beef
steps.text: Sauté the chuck and onion in another skillet over medium-high until the beef is cooked through, 5 minutes. Add the chili powder, cumin, ½ tsp salt, garlic and coriander and cook one minute more, until it smells right.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Warm the beans over low. Layer beans then beef into the shells and top with lettuce, olives, tomatoes, jalapeños and queso fresco.

steps.title: Squash first
steps.text: Put the squash, broth and honey in a 4–6 qt slow cooker, cover, and cook on high for 1½ hours — it needs a head start on the chops.

steps.title: Sear the chops
steps.text: Heat the oil in a sauté pan over medium-high until it shimmers and sear the chops 3–4 minutes a side. Set them aside.

steps.title: Cider onions
steps.text: Sauté the onion and garlic in the same pan for 3 minutes, deglaze with the cider, scraping the pan clean, and cook it nearly dry, 5 minutes.

steps.title: Finish in the cooker
steps.text: Spread the onions over the squash, lay the chops on top, cover, and cook on low about 1¼ hours, to 145° at the thickest point. Keep the chops warm.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Drain the squash through a sieve, tip it into a bowl, and mash it as coarse or smooth as you like. Stir in the sage and season.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Chops over the squash, with apple-cherry sauce alongside.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Oven to 400°. Spray two 1½-cup baking dishes, or one 3-cup dish.

steps.title: Mix and chill the meatballs
steps.text: Combine the chicken, ¼ cup onion, bread crumbs, Parmesan, parsley, basil and egg and season. Scoop into 18–20 tablespoon-sized meatballs and freeze them 10 minutes — ground chicken is slack, and the chill is what lets them hold together in the pan.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Heat 2 Tbsp oil in a sauté pan over medium until it shimmers and brown the meatballs in two batches, 2 minutes a side. Move them to a plate.

steps.title: Sauce and assemble
steps.text: Sauté ½ cup onion, the garlic and tomato paste in the same pan over medium-high for a minute, then stir in the crushed tomatoes and season. Divide the sauce and meatballs between the dishes and set them on a baking sheet. Brush the baguette slices with 1 Tbsp oil, add them to the sheet, and bake 7 minutes; flip the bread and bake 8 more. Lay a slice of baguette on each casserole and two slices of provolone over that.

steps.title: Broil
steps.text: Broiler to high, and broil just until the cheese melts.

steps.title: Butter the sheet
steps.text: Brush a large baking sheet with melted butter.

steps.title: Mix the custard
steps.text: Combine the eggs, milk, cream, granulated sugar, orange liqueur and mace.

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Dip the bread to coat both sides and lay the slices out in a single layer. Pour the rest of the custard over, cover, and refrigerate 2 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Hot oven, room-temperature bread
steps.text: Oven to 475°, and let the chilled slices come back to room temperature first or the centres stay wet.

steps.title: Bake, then broil
steps.text: 7–8 minutes, flip, then 7–8 more until puffed and golden. Finish under a high broiler with the rack 6 inches down, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Orange syrup
steps.text: Simmer the maple syrup, juice, butter and salt in a saucepan, then whisk the vanilla in off the heat.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Syrup over the toast, with almonds and powdered sugar.

steps.title: Butter the dish
steps.text: Oven to 350°. Brush a 9×13-inch baking dish with 2 Tbsp melted butter.

steps.title: Soften the peppers
steps.text: Melt the other 2 Tbsp butter in a nonstick skillet over medium and cook the bell peppers, scallion whites and jalapeño until soft, about 5 minutes. Let them cool to room temperature before they meet the eggs.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, cream, salt and black pepper together, fold in the peppers, cheese and scallion greens, and pour it into the dish.

steps.title: Bake and stir
steps.text: 10 minutes, then stir and bake 10–20 minutes more, until the eggs are set the way you like them. Serve out of a bowl.

steps.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps.text: Sauté the mushrooms in butter over medium-high until browned, 6–8 minutes, then add the onion and garlic for 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Paprika and tapioca
steps.text: Stir in the paprika, season with salt, black pepper and pepper flakes, and cook 2 minutes, stirring often. Add the roasted red peppers and 2 cups broth and bring it to a simmer, then whisk in the tapioca and cook 2 minutes more.

steps.title: Layer, do not stir
steps.text: Lay the reserved cobs in the bottom of the slow cooker — they give up more corn flavour than the kernels do. Add the mushroom mixture, then the corn kernels and bell pepper, then the last 2 cups of broth. Leave it unstirred.

steps.title: Slow cook
steps.text: Cover and cook 2½–3 hours on high or 4–5 on low. Pull the cobs out and stir.

steps.title: Blend the finish
steps.text: Purée the cilantro with the yogurt, buttermilk, lime juice and 2 cups of the cooked chowder until thick and creamy, then stir it back into the cooker.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scallions, lime wedges and a dusting of paprika on each bowl.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Oven to 400° and line a baking sheet with foil.

steps.title: Soak the bread
steps.text: Whisk the milk, eggs, salt, chili powder, pepper, oregano, cumin and coriander together, add the bread, and mash it to a paste with a fork. This panade is what keeps the loaves tender.

steps.title: Mince the vegetables
steps.text: Mince the onions, poblanos and garlic in a food processor.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Mix the ground chuck, ground pork, cilantro, minced vegetables and the bread mixture together.

steps.title: Shape and bake
steps.text: Divide into six portions of about 9 oz, shape them into mini loaves on the sheet, and bake to 165° in the centre, about 35 minutes. Rest them 10 minutes while the gravy comes together.

steps.title: Roux
steps.text: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium, whisk the flour in, and cook it 2 minutes.

steps.title: Milk gravy
steps.text: Whisk the milk in slowly until smooth, bring it to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes.

steps.title: Cheese off the heat
steps.text: Off the heat, whisk in the cheese, lime juice and zest until the cheese melts, then season with salt and cayenne. Keeping it off the burner stops it going grainy.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Gravy over the loaves.

steps.title: Cook the macaroni
steps.text: Oven to 350°. Boil the macaroni in salted water as the packet directs, then drain.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Cook the ground chuck, onion, carrots and garlic in a large saucepan over medium, stirring now and then, until the beef browns. Drain the fat and return it to the pan.

steps.title: Bloom the paprika
steps.text: Stir in the paprika, tomato paste, caraway seeds and marjoram, cover, and cook 5 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer, then bake
steps.text: Add the crushed and diced tomatoes, pimentos and vinegar, bring it to a simmer, and cook 20 minutes until the carrots give to a fork. Season, then stir in the Velveeta and macaroni. Tip it into a 9×13-inch dish and bake about 30 minutes, until the cheese melts through.

steps.title: Crisp the bacon
steps.text: Oven to 350°. Cook the bacon in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet until crisp, drain it, and mince it once cool.

steps.title: Sweat and flour
steps.text: Melt 3 Tbsp butter into the drippings over medium-low. Add the leeks, carrot, celery and cayenne, season, and sweat until the leeks soften, about 8 minutes. Sprinkle the flour over and stir it for a minute, then raise the heat to medium-high.

steps.title: Build the chowder
steps.text: Deglaze with the wine, scraping the pan, and cook a minute. Stir in the stock, cream, lemon juice and thyme and bring it to a simmer.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Stir in the hash browns and salmon and bring it back to a simmer. Set the skillet on a baking sheet and bake about 20 minutes, until it bubbles at the edges.

steps.title: Bacon crumbs
steps.text: Combine the panko, 1 Tbsp melted butter, the zest and the minced bacon.

steps.title: Broiler
steps.text: Broiler to high with the rack 6 inches from the element.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Scatter the crumbs over and broil about 2 minutes until golden, then parsley over the skillet.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium and cook the sausage until browned and cooked through, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Sweat and spice
steps.text: Add the onions and bell peppers and sweat until they start to soften, about 5 minutes, then the tomato paste, garlic, chili powder, cumin and oregano for one minute.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Stir in the broth, squash, tomatoes, kidney beans and black beans. Bring it to a boil, cover, drop to medium-low, and simmer about 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the squash gives to a fork.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the cilantro and season.

steps.title: Bacon, then chicken
steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large sauté pan over medium until crisp, about 15 minutes, and drain it. Pour off all but 2 Tbsp of the drippings, then sear the chicken over high until browned on both sides, about 4 minutes, and move it to a 4–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Mince and dry the base
steps.text: Pulse the onion, celery, carrot and garlic to a mince in a food processor, then sauté it in the drippings over medium-high until the liquid cooks off, 6–8 minutes.

steps.title: Deglaze and slow cook
steps.text: Deglaze with the wine and cook it nearly dry, 2 minutes. Add the broth, bring it to a boil, and tip it into the cooker. Cover and cook on high 1½ hours, until the chicken is fork-tender. Lift the chicken out, chop it, return it, and stir in the tomatoes and romaine — the lettuce goes in at the end so it only just wilts.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Bacon, croutons and Parmesan aioli on each bowl.

steps.title: Sear the pork
steps.text: Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a sauté pan over medium-high and sear the pork on all sides, 2–3 minutes a side. Move it to a 4–6 qt slow cooker.

steps.title: Soften the vegetables
steps.text: Sauté the onion, celery and fennel in the last spoon of oil in the same pan over medium-high until softened, 5–7 minutes, and add them to the cooker.

steps.title: Long cook, then shred
steps.text: Add the broth and thyme, cover, and cook 4–5 hours on high or 8–9 on low. Lift the pork out, shred it once it is cool enough to handle, and discard the bone. Strain the cooking liquid — it is worth keeping, and boiling pasta in it is the best use for it.

steps.title: Brown the skin
steps.text: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high and cook the chicken skin-side down until browned, 3–4 minutes.

steps.title: Four hours
steps.text: Put the broth, celery, carrots, onion, thyme and bay leaves in a 4–6 qt slow cooker and lay the chicken on top, skin up. Cover and cook on high 4 hours, until tender, then move the chicken to a board to cool a little.

steps.title: Noodles last
steps.text: Add the noodles to the cooker, cover, and cook 10 minutes until tender. Strip the skin, fat and bones off the chicken, shred the meat back into the soup, and season. Scallions and lemon zest over each bowl.

steps.title: Slow cook the brisket
steps.text: Stir the water, beer and pickling spice into a 4–6 qt slow cooker — use your own spice if the corned beef came without a packet. Cover and cook until fork-tender, 3 hours on high or up to 6 on low. Rest the brisket 5 minutes before slicing.

steps.title: Quick slaw
steps.text: Whisk the vinegar and sugar together, toss the onion, carrot and pepper rings through it, and season. Leave it 5 minutes, until slightly wilted.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Butter one side of each bread slice and spread ½ Tbsp dressing on the other. Lay 3 oz of corned beef on the dressed side of eight slices.

steps.title: Close
steps.text: Slaw, then a slice of cheese, then the remaining bread dressing-side down.

steps.title: Griddle
steps.text: Heat a griddle or panini press to medium and grill about 5 minutes total, until the bread is crisp and the cheese has melted.

steps.title: Fry the potatoes
steps.text: Oven to 400°. Sauté the potatoes in butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high for 5 minutes, add the bell pepper and onion for 3 more, then stir in the ham.

steps.title: Scramble and chill
steps.text: Whisk 11 eggs with the chives, add them to the skillet, and scramble constantly until nearly set; season. Off the heat, stir in the cream cheese and orange juice until smooth, then chill the filling while you handle the pastry — warm filling will melt it.

steps.title: Fill and braid
steps.text: Unfold one pastry sheet on a floured surface and roll it to 10×12 inches. Move it onto a sheet of parchment, trim it, spoon half the filling down the centre, and braid the sides over. Repeat with the second sheet, then lift both on their parchment onto baking sheets.

steps.title: Egg wash
steps.text: Beat the last egg with the water and brush it over the tops.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Parmesan over the top, then 20–30 minutes until golden. Cool 5 minutes.

steps.title: Sweat the vegetables
steps.text: Sweat the mushrooms, carrot, celery, onion and garlic in oil in a pot over medium until slightly softened, 3 minutes.

steps.title: Noodles in the broth
steps.text: Add the broth, bring it to a simmer over medium-high, stir the noodles in, and cook them as the packet directs. Stir in the chicken, tarragon and chives and season.

steps.title: Brown in two batches
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high and brown the pork on all sides in two batches; set it aside. Drop to medium, add the onions, and sweat them covered until soft, 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin, oregano, coriander and bay leaf for a minute.

steps.title: Two hours
steps.text: Stir in the broth, tomato sauce, diced tomatoes, chipotle, adobo sauce and the pork and bring it to a boil. Cover, drop to low, and simmer about 2 hours until the pork is tender.

steps.title: Hominy last
steps.text: Add the hominy, cilantro and lime juice and season.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Radishes and avocado over the top.

steps.title: Soften the apples
steps.text: Microwave the apples with the brandy until softened, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Mix the braising liquid
steps.text: Whisk the apple butter, broth, wine and vinegar together and set it aside.

steps.title: Brown the turkey
steps.text: Melt the butter in a large sauté pan over medium-high and brown the turkey skin-side down, 8–10 minutes. Set it aside.

steps.title: Forty cloves
steps.text: Sauté the onion and garlic in the same pan until soft, about 5 minutes, then add the sage and season.

steps.title: Layer and cook
steps.text: Drain the apples, keeping the brandy for something else. Layer the apples, onions and garlic into a 4–6 qt slow cooker, then the apple butter mixture, the chile and the turkey. Cover and cook on high 3–4 hours, to 165° at the thickest part.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Tent the turkey under foil. Strain the garlic mixture and discard the liquid — the solids are the spread.

steps.title: Blend the spread
steps.text: Purée the garlic mixture with the zest and lemon juice until smooth and season. Serve with baguette and minced sage.
